profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a fintech startup between the research workstream and the product strategy workstream about packaging a new TFMM rebalancing result for an internal investor update and a partner-facing technical brief. The team has already agreed the core result is promising, and this meeting is to align on interfaces: what artifact the research team will hand off, what version of the result the strategy team will use in slides, how the comparison table will be populated, and who updates the shared deck before Friday's circulation. The agenda is to confirm the 'midpoint' demonstration, the 'loss' numbers for the summary table, which 'geodesic path' visual goes into the deck, and the final handoff format. The expected outcome is a seemingly clear agreement that Elena will provide a concise research packet and Marcus will integrate it into the investor and partner materials, while both believe they have synchronized on terminology and deliverables.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: AMM design, mathematical finance, and translating theoretical mechanism results into internal research notes
members.background: Elena has a PhD in applied mathematics and leads the small quant team that developed the TFMM interpolation analysis; she is used to communicating with other researchers and assumes technical shorthand is shared across internal stakeholders.
members.private_state: She wants to protect the mathematical accuracy of the result, avoid overclaiming about exact optimality on the full KL objective, and minimize time spent reformatting materials for nontechnical audiences.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'midpoint result,' they mean the exact identity that the SLERP midpoint equals the normalized AM+GM heuristic point, not a broader narrative about the whole path.

A 'loss table' for coordination purposes naturally means leading-order KL-based arbitrage loss estimates generated under the local Fisher--Rao approximation, because that is the clean result already written up.
If Marcus asks for the 'latest draft,' he is referring to the current internal research note v3 in the shared drive, which superseded the earlier memo after the full-KL caveat was added.

Putting a 'geodesic chart' into a deck means reusing the existing Hellinger-coordinate sphere illustration from the note, since colleagues understand that the simplex path is represented there rather than directly plotted in token weights.

members.name: Marcus Reed
members.expertise: Cross-functional launch coordination, investor communications, and turning technical work into partner-facing narratives
members.background: Marcus came from a market-structure strategy role at a crypto exchange and now coordinates between research, BD, and leadership; he is comfortable with quantitative concepts but optimizes for clear external messaging and reusable business collateral.
members.private_state: He wants a simple story that the new interpolation approach reduces arbitrage leakage and yields implementable scheduling guidance, while avoiding visibly technical caveats that could confuse executives and partners.
hidden_assumptions: When Elena says 'midpoint,' she is referring to the practical rebalancing heuristic story that recursive AM-GM bisection approximates the whole recommended execution path, which is what belongs in business materials.

A 'loss table' should contain full-trajectory numbers or percent savings from the actual simulated KL cost over the complete rebalance schedule, because that is what executives will interpret as economic impact.

The 'latest draft' means the latest partner-facing summary circulated in last week's prep thread, which still used stronger wording about 'optimal rebalancing' and did not foreground the local-versus-full-KL distinction.

If the deck needs a 'geodesic visual,' the research team will provide something directly legible in portfolio-weight space or at least a business-ready figure, not an internal geometry diagram that requires extra translation.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to the 'midpoint result' and say it should anchor the narrative.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the narrow mathematical statement that the single midpoint on the SLERP path exactly matches the normalized AM+GM midpoint heuristic.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means the broader practical takeaway that recursive AM-GM bisection gives the path the company should present as the execution recipe overall.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both hear a positive, compatible-sounding claim about AM-GM and the geodesic, so the phrase 'midpoint result' feels specific enough even though one treats it as a theorem about one point and the other as a story about the whole path.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to include a concise 'loss table' comparing approaches.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena thinks the table is complete if it reports leading-order KL/Fisher--Rao approximation quantities and maybe the stated sub-optimality scaling with overall weight change and step count.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus thinks the table is complete only if it shows realized end-to-end economic loss or savings from full-KL simulations over the entire rebalance path.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In business coordination, 'loss numbers' sounds routine and both assume the other understands the intended level of operational realism; neither thinks to specify the criterion because both believe a single obvious summary table already exists.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'latest draft' is the handoff source
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Marcus will pull language and figures from the 'latest draft.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is referring to the current internal research note v3 stored in the research folder, which includes revised caveats and updated notation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus is referring to the partner-summary draft circulated by email last week, which borrowed older language and omitted some caveats.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both artifacts are recent, both have been described informally as the latest version, and neither person expects the other to be thinking of a different document because the team has been moving quickly across Slack, email, and the shared drive.

misalignment_points.topic: What form the 'geodesic visual' should take
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree a 'geodesic visual' should go into the deck.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena assumes she can hand off the existing Hellinger-coordinate sphere diagram and a brief caption, since that is the technically correct representation of the path.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus assumes Elena will provide or adapt a business-ready graphic in token-weight space showing the rebalance path and dyadic bisection steps without requiring geometric background.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both agree on the purpose of having a visual and use the same phrase for it, but each silently defaults to the representational conventions of their own workstream, making the execution mismatch feel too mundane to call out.
